draws.rationale: The experiment reads the HMMER full-sequence e-value strictly as the statistical significance of the profile match — the exact quantity the instrument directly computes and is validated to report — with no leap to homology, orthology, or function.
draws.right_instrument: hmmer (profile search) reporting the best full-sequence e-value as significance

draws.rationale: A significant profile-HMM e-value is the statistical significance of similarity, a reliable screen, but not itself proof of biological homology/function and can be inflated by composition/low-complexity bias, leaving a residual gap to reality.
draws.right_instrument: HMMER profile search (as named) — correct as a homology-significance screen, with survivors confirmed downstream

draws.rationale: The experiment reads the e-value strictly as a similarity-significance screen (a clean no-hit at threshold), which is exactly what the instrument directly measures within its validated in-regime use — no homology/function inference is claimed.
draws.right_instrument: BLAST / HMMER local sequence-homology search with Karlin-Altschul e-value statistics

draws.rationale: A clean no-hit result is a direct read of the search's own significance outcome — the e-value screen at the stated cutoff IS the answer to the negative-similarity claim, and it avoids the known homology/remote-homology gap by staying within the significance-screen envelope.
draws.right_instrument: BLAST / HMMER local sequence-homology search with Karlin-Altschul e-value statistics

draws.rationale: A clean no-hit result read strictly as 'no significant homolog at this cutoff' is a direct in-regime read of the search's own significance output, not a homology/function inference that reality could correct.
draws.right_instrument: BLAST / HMMER local sequence-homology search with Karlin-Altschul e-value statistics

draws.rationale: The experiment reads the e-value strictly as its native quantity — a relative similarity-significance screen for ranking two queries — which is exactly what the tool directly measures in-regime, not an inferred homology/function claim.
draws.right_instrument: BLAST / HMMER e-value similarity-significance screen

draws.rationale: The experiment reads the e-value strictly as a relative similarity-significance screen — exactly the quantity Karlin-Altschul statistics directly compute — and makes no claim of homology, function, or remote similarity, so the in-regime output IS the answer.
draws.right_instrument: BLAST / HMMER local sequence-homology search with Karlin-Altschul e-value statistics

draws.rationale: The experiment reads the e-value strictly as relative similarity-significance to rank two queries against a valid DB, which is exactly the quantity BLAST/HMMER directly computes and validates — no homology/function inference crosses the H5 gap.
draws.right_instrument: BLAST / HMMER local sequence-homology search with Karlin-Altschul e-value statistics

draws.rationale: A BLAST/HMMER e-value measures statistical significance of sequence similarity, which cannot establish orthology or shared molecular function — exactly the out-of-regime homology/function claim the instrument's known gap (H5) forbids.
draws.right_instrument: none — route to human/real experiment (experimental functional characterization plus phylogenetic orthology inference; sequence search alone cannot deliver this)

draws.rationale: A BLAST/HMMER e-value measures statistical significance of sequence similarity, not biological homology, orthology, or shared molecular function, so it cannot faithfully model the functional-ortholog claim.
draws.right_instrument: none — route to human/real experiment (functional homology requires phylogenetic orthology inference plus experimental functional characterization)

draws.rationale: The experiment reads a similarity-significance e-value as proof of orthology and identical molecular function, which is the tool's explicitly stated known gap (H5) and out-of-regime.
draws.right_instrument: none — route to human/real experiment (functional homology requires phylogenetic orthology inference plus experimental functional characterization, not a pairwise e-value)

draws.rationale: A raw pairwise BLAST e-value is mathematically incapable of detecting remote homology between sequences lacking significant pairwise similarity — this is the instrument's own declared out-of-regime H5 gap.
draws.right_instrument: profile-based remote-homology search (HMMER profile-HMM or PSI-BLAST), and even then only as a screen requiring confirmation

draws.rationale: A raw pairwise BLAST e-value cannot detect remote homology between sequences with no significant pairwise similarity — this is the instrument's own known gap (H5), so it cannot faithfully model the experiment at all.
draws.right_instrument: a profile-HMM search (HMMER against a profile/HMM database) for remote-homology detection

draws.rationale: A raw pairwise BLAST e-value cannot detect remote homology between sequences lacking significant pairwise similarity — this is explicitly out-of-regime and its known gap (H5).
draws.right_instrument: a profile-HMM / HMMER (or PSI-BLAST) remote-homology search, plus structural/experimental confirmation for a homology claim

draws.rationale: The experiment reads a low-complexity/composition-biased e-value as true biological similarity, which is exactly the H5 out-of-regime failure the instrument's statistics cannot correct for.
draws.right_instrument: none — route to human/real experiment

draws.rationale: A low e-value driven by a low-complexity/repeat-rich region is exactly the composition-bias artifact the instrument's own known gap (H5) flags — it cannot distinguish this from true biological similarity, so its output is not trustworthy here.
draws.right_instrument: none — route to human/real experiment (with low-complexity masking e.g. DUST/SEG plus expert review)

draws.rationale: A low e-value driven by a low-complexity/repeat-rich region read as true biological similarity is the instrument's explicitly stated out-of-regime failure mode (H5), where composition bias inflates significance the raw e-value cannot distinguish from real similarity.
draws.right_instrument: none — route to human/real experiment

draws.rationale: Asserting proven common ancestry (homology) from an e-value is exactly the tool's known out-of-regime gap: the e-value measures statistical significance of similarity, not established homology.
draws.right_instrument: none — route to human/real experiment

draws.rationale: The experiment asserts biological homology/common ancestry as established fact from an e-value, which measures statistical significance of similarity only — an out-of-regime claim the instrument's known gap (H5) explicitly forbids.
draws.right_instrument: none — route to human/real experiment

draws.rationale: Asserting proven common ancestry (homology as fact) from an e-value is explicitly out-of-regime: the tool measures statistical significance of similarity, not homology.
draws.right_instrument: none — route to human/real experiment

draws.rationale: A significant e-value against a partial database is a similarity screen and can never establish the absolute absence of homologs anywhere in nature — both the homology claim and the completeness claim lie outside the instrument's regime.
draws.right_instrument: none — route to human/real experiment

draws.rationale: A significant e-value against a partial database is statistical significance of similarity to indexed sequences and cannot support an absolute claim of no homologs anywhere in nature — both the homology inference and the completeness assertion lie outside the tool's validity.
draws.right_instrument: none — route to human/real experiment

draws.rationale: A significant e-value against a partial database is a similarity screen and can never establish the absence of any homolog anywhere in nature — an absolute-completeness claim the instrument is definitionally unable to support.
draws.right_instrument: none — route to human/real experiment
